cards.label: flow replays at parity across 4 runs (155 flows x mock, SQL, mock-container, SQL-container)
failing flows in the final runs
per-flow data-state checks equal after mutating flows (pages and/or sqlcmd dumps; 30 mutating flows per run, unchecked ones covered by the end-of-sequence snapshots, all equal)
regressions (SQL-mode WebForms edit + save-time validation), PR #91
known divergences per run, all host 404 error-page bodies (status equal)

paragraphs: The legacy apps (.NET Framework 4.7.2 code built and hosted on Mono 6.12 + xsp4, because the VM has no Windows/IIS) and the migrated ASP.NET Core 8 apps were run side by side and every one of the 155 recorded transcripts was replayed live against both, in lockstep, with both sides restarted before every mutation sequence.

Mock mode: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known; 17/17 per-flow data-state checks (page snapshots where the baseline took them; the other 13 mutating flows are not re-rendered to keep mock navigation properties cold, Q4) and 9/9 end-of-sequence snapshots equal. Same result against the .NET 8 Linux container images: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known.

SQL mode: legacy MVC and WebForms (EF6 on Mono) and .NET 8 (EF Core 8) each seeded a fresh database in the same SQL Server 2022 container from their own initializer. The first round found 6 failing flows from 2 root causes, both in the migrated WebForms SQL path; after the fix: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known, 30/30 per-flow data-state checks equal including sqlcmd dumps of both databases after every mutating flow. Container SQL profile (compose images and their own sqldata container, sqlcmd dumps of both databases): 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known, 30/30 per-flow data-state checks equal.
Every remaining difference is classified in section 10. Open regressions: 0. Not verified here: Windows/IIS hosting of the legacy apps, and a recorded manual UI walkthrough (see section 11).

tests.notes: 2 skipped = SQL Server-backed EF tests, enabled by ESHOP_TEST_SQL_CONNECTION
WebApplicationFactory: transcript parity tests for both apps, BinaryFormatter, WebForms save validation, smoke

Transcript suite is the legacy test suite: 155 flows replayed live against legacy in each run; legacy-live vs recorded baseline: mock 155/155 identical or equivalent; SQL 130 identical/equivalent + 25 documented SQL-mode differences (L-01, L-02)

tests.suite: Lockstep transcript replay, 4 runs x 155 flows

differences.flows: wf-edit-postback-valid (+ cascaded data-state diffs in wf-edit-after-details, wf-edit-postback-price-nonnumeric) - SQL mode only
differences.root_cause: Round 1: legacy 302, .NET 8 500. The Razor Pages Edit handler loads the item with FindCatalogItem (EF Core tracks it) and then passes a separately bound CatalogItem with the same key to UpdateCatalogItem, which did db.Entry(item).State = Modified -> EF Core InvalidOperationException (another instance with the same key is already tracked). EF6 on legacy tolerated the pattern. File: eShopNet8/src/eShop.Catalog.Infrastructure/Data/CatalogService.cs (UpdateCatalogItem), caller eShopNet8/src/eShopNet8.WebForms/Pages/Catalog/Edit.cshtml.cs.
differences.status: Fixed in https://github.com/COG-GTM/eShopModernizing/pull/91: the already-tracked copy is detached before the posted entity is attached. Unit test Update_after_find_in_the_same_scope_replaces_the_tracked_copy. SQL replay after fix: parity, data state equal.

differences.flows: wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range (+ cascaded data-state diffs in wf-create-postback-price-nonnumeric, wf-create-postback-no-viewstate) - SQL mode only
differences.root_cause: Round 1: legacy 500, .NET 8 302 and the row was saved. Q8 means the WebForms validators do not block the postback, but in SQL mode legacy EF6 DbContext.SaveChanges validates DataAnnotations (DbEntityValidationException for Stock 20000000 > 10 million) so nothing is stored; EF Core performs no save-time validation. The WebForms model has its own annotations (eShopLegacyWebFormsSolution/src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogItem.cs, Q9: Name not required, wide Price range) that differ from MVC's. Files: eShopNet8/src/eShop.Catalog.Infrastructure/Data/CatalogService.cs.
differences.status: Fixed in https://github.com/COG-GTM/eShopModernizing/pull/91: ICatalogItemSaveValidator runs before Add/Update in the EF service (MVC annotations by default, WebFormsCatalogItemSaveValidator with the legacy WebForms annotations registered by the Razor Pages app). Tests Save_validates_the_legacy_annotations_like_EF6_and_stores_nothing and WebFormsSaveValidationTests. SQL replay after fix: parity, data state equal.

differences.root_cause: Status 404 equal; legacy body is the Mono/xsp4 host HttpException error page (Mono version + stack trace), ASP.NET Core returns an empty 404. Host-generated, not app code. eShopNet8/tests/eShopNet8.IntegrationTests/Parity/known-divergences.json.
/api stays 404 on both (Q1, legacy CatalogController2 never discovered); only the Mono host 404 page body differs.
/items/abc/pic does not match items/{catalogItemId:int}/pic: 404 on both; Mono host error page body differs.
Unmapped WebForms URL: 404 and content type equal; Mono/xsp4 host error page text differs from the Razor Pages 404.

differences.flows: wf-create-* (SQL container run with both compose services up): wf-create-postback-valid, wf-create-after-list, wf-create-after-details, wf-create-postback-name-missing, wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range, wf-create-postback-price-nonnumeric, wf-create-postback-no-viewstate
differences.root_cause: In the compose SQL profile webforms-sql depends_on mvc-sql, so both .NET 8 apps share one DB and mvc-sql seeds it first; the WebForms process then takes a fresh HiLo block and the created item gets id 21 instead of legacy's 13 (legacy is replayed one app per DB). The id shift cascades into the data-state diff and into wf-create-after-details (it requests the legacy id 13 -> Q7 500). Same rows otherwise. Observed in two container runs (7 and 7 failing).
differences.status: Not a product difference (HiLo blocks are per process by design, legacy EF6 HiLo behaves the same). Final container SQL run uses NET8_DOCKER_SOLO=1 (start-net8.sh: up --no-deps, one app at a time) and is reported in section 5.

differences.flows: SQL mode, legacy-live vs recorded (mock) baseline: mvc-details-cold-12, mvc-delete-cold-10, mvc-index-negative-page, mvc-index-negative-size, mvc-edit-post-unknown-id, mvc-delete-post-unknown-id
differences.root_cause: Legacy itself behaves differently in SQL mode (Q18, BASELINE.md section 5): EF lazy loading fills cold navigation properties; negative paging and POST unknown id throw (500) in EF but not in the mock. The .NET 8 app reproduces each identically (pair verdict equivalent).

differences.flows: SQL mode, WebForms legacy-live vs mock baseline: wf-index-* / wf-details-found* / wf-edit-found / wf-delete-found / *-warm-list (prices rendered 19.50 instead of 19.5), wf-details-cold-1 and wf-delete-cold-3 (200 instead of 500), wf-index-negative-page (500), wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range (500)
differences.root_cause: First observation of legacy WebForms in SQL mode (new in this stage): SQL decimal(18,2) keeps scale 2 so Price.ToString() renders 19.50; lazy loading avoids the cold-mock NRE (Q4); EF Skip with a negative count throws; EF6 save-time validation (see R-02). Legacy mode differences, extension of Q18 to WebForms. .NET 8 reproduces each identically.

Legacy /api/files serialises with BinaryFormatter (CWE-502 deserialisation risk, removed from .NET 8). The .NET 8 app keeps the endpoint shape with a safe replacement; the replay compares it equivalent after normalisation and BinaryFormatterTests assert BinaryFormatter is not used.
differences.status: Intentional, documented in INVENTORY.md Q2 (no observable pair difference)

differences.flows: Q3 mvc-api-brand-delete-*; Q4 *-cold-*; Q5 mvc-index-size0, wf-index-size0, wf-index-nonnumeric; Q6 mvc-delete-post-unknown-id; Q7 wf-details-missing, wf-details-aspx-no-route, wf-edit-missing, wf-delete-missing, wf-delete-after-details; Q8 wf-create-postback-*; Q9/Q11/Q13/Q15/Q16 markup and XML negotiation
differences.root_cause: Legacy defects catalogued in modernization/INVENTORY.md (DELETE /api/brands no-op 200, cold mock navigation properties, pageSize=0 divide-by-zero, unknown ids 500, WebForms ModelState vs Page.IsValid, annotation drift, pager count, stray </a>, XML content negotiation). Kept on purpose so the migration is behaviour-preserving; every one replays at parity.
differences.status: Reproduced identically (deliberately preserved); candidates for post-migration fixes

differences.root_cause: Legacy reference runs on Mono/xsp4, not IIS/.NET Framework on Windows, with documented shims in throwaway copies (case-sensitive asset copies, MVC 5.2.7 Razor refs, WebForms ScriptManager/ModelState/binding/SelectMethod shims, HiLo script paths, connection strings). Windows-only behaviour (IIS error pages, Windows auth, registry/LocalDB) is not observed.

In the container SQL run the .NET 8 apps use the compose profile's own sqldata container (host port 1434), so the legacy DB (host SQL Server 2022 container, port 1433) and the .NET 8 DB are in two containers from the same image rather than one; sqlcmd dumps of both were taken after every mutating flow (--sql-server-net8 127.0.0.1,1434) and were equal. The single-container requirement is met by the local SQL run.
differences.status: Accepted (compose profile owns its SQL Server)
